Exercise A

Grandma's Childhood

Read what Lena's grandmother says about growing up. Choose the correct word for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading Text

"When I was your age," says Lena's grandmother, "we used to play outside until it got dark. There was no internet, so we didn't use to spend hours looking at a screen."

"My family 1 one television, and we all watched the same programme together in the evening."

"If I wanted to talk to a friend, I couldn't just send a 2 — I had to call their house and hope someone answered."

"We used a paper 3 when we went on holiday, because there was no GPS to guide us."

"Music came from the 4 or from cassette tapes, not from an app."

"To do 5, we went to the library and looked things up in real books, not on a search engine."

"Honestly, I think we spent much more time 6 than teenagers do today."

Exercise B

used to / didn't use to

Complete the sentences about the past with used to or didn't use to.

Complete the Sentence

1. People write letters instead of sending emails.

2. Children have smartphones — they simply didn't exist.

3. My grandad repair his own radio when it broke.

4. Families have the internet at home before the 1990s.

5. People meet friends in person much more often.

6. Students type their homework on a computer — they wrote it by hand.

7. My mum listen to the radio every morning before school.

8. Shops accept online payments — everyone paid with cash.

Exercise C

used to vs. Simple Past

Choose used to for repeated past habits, or the simple past for a single, finished action.

Complete the Sentence

1. My grandmother to school every day when she was young.

2. Yesterday, she to the shop to buy some bread.

3. Last week, our class a museum about old technology.

4. In the 1980s, people songs from the radio onto cassette tapes.

5. Grandad a letter to his brother every single month for years.

6. He his last letter to him in 1995.

7. Before computers, workers typewriters in almost every office.

8. On that day, the reporter to finish the story before the deadline.

Exercise D

Writing: Life Before Smartphones

Interview an older family member (or imagine their answers) and write 6–8 sentences about what life was like before smartphones. Use at least three examples of used to / didn't use to.

Think about these questions

• How did people use to keep in touch with friends?

• What did people use to do in their free time?

• What didn't use to exist that we have today?

• What do you think was better or worse back then?

You can use these: People used to ... We didn't use to ... My grandparents used to ... There didn't use to be ...
Your text
Aim for 6–8 sentences with at least three examples of used to / didn't use to.
